analysis.title: China: a broad weakening in October data
key_insights: China's October activity data weakened across the board and missed consensus by a wide margin, pointing to weaker domestic demand and a larger gap between supply and demand indicators, with property strain continuing and policy support still incremental.

Retail sales growth (nominal) slowed to 0.4% YoY in October from 1.1% in September, below the 0.8% consensus. A base effect contributed: the National Day holiday was 7 days in 2026 against 8 days in 2025. Jewellery sales fell 28.7% and auto sales fell 21.4%.

YTD fixed asset investment (FAI) fell 8.1% YoY in October from -7.2% in September. The report's own calculation puts October alone at -16.1% YoY, the sharpest drop since February 2020. Tertiary-sector FAI is -10.9% YTD, manufacturing FAI -2.9% YTD and infrastructure FAI -7.3% YTD.

Industrial production growth slowed to 4.8% YoY from 5.5%, below the 5.3% consensus. Auto manufacturing slowed to 0.9% from 6.7%. High-tech manufacturing accelerated to 17.6% from 15.3%, and IC output growth rose to 21.9% from 18.4%.

The property sector worsened. Property investment is -21.6% YTD (from -20.6%), and monthly property FAI is -34.2% YoY. Developers' funding fell 28.0% YoY in the month. New home prices fell 0.2% MoM in 70 cities, though the YoY decline narrowed to -2.7% from -3.0%.

Trade stayed strong. Exports grew 35.2% YoY and imports 41.6%. The trade surplus was USD105.3bn in October and USD1,051bn over 10M26. Much of the value growth comes from price inflation: IC export prices rose 143.0% while IC export volume fell 2.4%.

Inflation is driven by imported energy and tech inputs. CPI was 0.7% YoY and core CPI 0.8%. PPI accelerated to 5.7% YoY. The widening PPI-CPI gap points to squeezed margins at mid- and downstream firms because upstream costs are not passed through.

Credit was weak. New aggregate financing was RMB1,151bn against RMB1,448bn consensus. RMB loans fell RMB100bn, with household loans down RMB430bn. Net government bond issuance rose to RMB1,184bn from RMB485bn a year earlier.
NBS manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 from 50.1, below the 49.9 consensus. The services PMI was 50.0 and the construction PMI 48.0 (from 50.3). The surveyed unemployment rate eased to 5.1% from 5.2%.

Policy easing so far has been incremental: RMB1.3trn of special CGBs and RMB800bn of policy-bank financing tools were fully issued by October, the local government issuance quota was raised by RMB550bn, and the PBoC switched its policy rate anchor to overnight, which lowers short-term money market rates by about 15bp. The PBoC also raised the FX deposit RRR by 2%. The bank sees limited evidence in the data so far.

For 2027 the bank expects less supportive trade because the global AI capex cycle should slow and the US may tighten export controls and pursue the Section 301 overcapacity investigation. It expects China to keep a 4.5-5.0% growth target and sees more policy effort as necessary, but does not expect a meaningful scale-up of fiscal expansion.

Xi and Trump are expected to meet at APEC (18-19 November, Shenzhen) and possibly at the G20 (14-15 December, Miami) to discuss extending the Busan trade truce, which suspends US affiliate-rule export controls and China's rare earth export controls.

sector_views.rationale: Property investment, developer funding and sales volumes all remain in double-digit contraction, and the presales rule tightening restrains developer funding.
High-tech IP growth accelerated to 17.6% and high-tech FAI grew 4.0% YTD, offsetting weakness elsewhere.

earnings_insights: The bank flags stress on mid- and downstream corporate earnings in China because the PPI-CPI gap is widening and upstream raw material inflation is not passing through to finished goods.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Below the 0.8% consensus and down from 1.1%, showing weak consumption demand.
Deeper than -7.2% in September and below expectations of modest improvement. The bank's own monthly calculation is -16.1% YoY.
Below the 5.3% consensus and down from 5.5%, but still solid and outpacing demand indicators.
Market consensus for October IP growth, which the print missed.
Market expectation for October retail sales growth, which the print missed.
Down from 5.2%, the one bright spot in the activity data.
Down from 0.9% and slightly below expectations. Core CPI is 0.8%, and food deflation of -2.9% outweighs energy inflation of 9.9%.
Up from 5.0%, driven by upstream mining and raw materials, while downstream sectors stay deflationary.
Back in contraction, down from 50.1 and well below the 49.9 consensus.
Missed the RMB1,448bn consensus. New RMB loans were negative while net government bond issuance rose.
Slightly below expectations. Growth is driven by tech price inflation and refined fuels.
Above expectations, driven by tech and energy import price inflation rather than volume.
The bank thinks the government will more likely keep this target than lower it to around 4.5%.

risk_factors: Further weakening of domestic demand as property strain continues.

Slow fiscal execution, Beijing's requirement to avoid overinvestment and excess competition, and government reshuffling ahead of the 21st Party Congress in October 2027 could hold back policy support.
The global AI capex cycle slows in 2027, reducing demand for Asia's AI hardware exports.
Renewed US-China trade tension, with further US chip export controls raising the probability of Chinese retaliation with its own export controls.
Stress on mid- and downstream corporate earnings from limited pass-through of upstream cost inflation.
Weak household income growth and a negative wealth effect hold back consumption.
geopolitical: Xi and Trump are expected to meet at APEC (18-19 November, Shenzhen) and possibly the G20 (14-15 December, Miami) to discuss extending the Busan trade truce.
The truce suspends US export controls (the affiliate rule) and China's export controls on rare earths.
The US Section 301 investigation on manufacturing overcapacity could conclude at any time.
The Nvidia shakeup has revived US political momentum for stricter export controls on advanced chips to China.
The Democrats swept the US midterm elections, which could mean renewed trade tensions and tighter export controls, although Trump keeps executive power over trade policy.
EU import quota restrictions on Chinese EVs are coming.
Heightened geopolitical uncertainty and an energy shock are raising energy prices and China's fuel trade values.
